A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLSGE research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching the PCOD derivation from Appendix B in v1 to Appendix C in v2.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original gaze-estimation experiments across four transfer tasks, including backbone comparisons, ablations, visualizations, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, and Appendix A.3 adds experiments using only 100 unlabeled target images.

M1.justification: The truncated-Gaussian reweighting, PCOD alignment, marginal alignment, reweighted prediction loss, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Newly discussed distribution families and applications are possibilities, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four transfers from ETH-XGaze/Gaze360 to MPIIFaceGaze/EyeDiap. The new 100-image experiment changes sample size within existing coverage; proposed extensions such as pose estimation are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain identical comparator memberships. New Table 8 reuses the existing ResNet-18 and PnP-GA+ results alongside the sample-budget experiment, introducing no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 adds a ResNet-18 evaluation condition using 100 unlabeled target samples on the four retained tasks. The newly stated default 10%/10%/80% split documents previously unspecified settings; it does not establish that the existing experiments changed.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 tests whether performance depends on using more target data, comparing the original budget with 100 samples. The component ablations, visualization analysis, and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state five repeated evaluations and report averages, with identical uncertainty entries in Tables 2 and 3. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds 100-sample GLSGE errors of 5.47, 6.38, 5.65, and 7.41 degrees, averaging 6.23 degrees. These are newly reported results under a smaller sample budget; the original results in Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–5 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical method and PCOD derivation are retained, with the latter moved from Appendix B to C. Remark 3.1, new Appendix B, and the notation table explain existing mathematics and the factorization choice without adding a substantive formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same GLS perspective, correction framework, continuous reweighting, PCOD, and performance claims. The four headline error-reduction percentages are unchanged.

C2.justification: Remark 3.1 and Appendix B explain the chosen joint-distribution factorization. Other additions discuss alternative label distributions, possible extensions beyond gaze, and target-data costs; Appendix A.3 attributes most low-data degradation to conditional alignment. The previous limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly specifies 10% target training, 10% validation, and 80% testing, including 4,500 MPIIFaceGaze and 1,667 EyeDiap training images. Table 7 documents comparator sample budgets. Existing architecture, optimizer, hyperparameter, and hardware details are unchanged.

R1.justification: All 50 references and the central positioning against DG/UDA methods are retained. Appendix A.3 adds resource-based positioning through target-sample budgets and discussion of PnP-GA+'s augmentation and auxiliary-model requirements.

P1.justification: Section 2 gains numbered subsections, Section 3 gains a roadmap, and targeted explanatory passages and acknowledgements are added. Affiliation, conference-header, and language edits are limited; most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Several main-text layouts are substantially reworked: Figures 1, 2, and 5 become smaller text-wrapped displays, Tables 2–3 sit beside prose, and Figure 4 is relocated. V2 also adds notation Table 6 and appendix Tables 7–8, while retaining the original diagram and plot content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency by disclosing target-data splits and comparator budgets, and adds a useful low-data sensitivity experiment plus clearer modeling rationale. The benefit is limited by the new SOTA wording: Table 8 lists 6.23 degrees for 100-sample GLSGE and 6.20 degrees for PnP-GA+, with unequal training resources. The core method and headline results remain unchanged.
